title: Harness session transcripts are invisible to the transcript corpus and unusable for postmortems
wanted_capability: Three facets: (1) a transcript adapter so in-process harness sessions (brodex/glm/deepseek/minimax) are locatable and indexed — today every harness task has transcript_location=null, TRANSCRIPT_SEARCH roots don't cover the session dir, and bbox_search/bbox_cite/bbox_messages cannot see any bro work; (2) per-item timestamps or a sidecar append-only event log — session files are resume-state snapshots (Responses item shape, no timestamps, rewritten by compaction), so time-based postmortems of where a bro spent its run are impossible from disk; (3) BRO_HOME routing — the daemon does not export BRO_HOME to the in-process harness, so sessions land in the fallback ~/.bro-harness/sessions (2,224 files) instead of BRO_HOME/harness-sessions, off the documented state layout.
fallback_used: Usage-ledger arithmetic (turns/elapsed/fresh-tokens) + task-store last-50 events for postmortems; find(1) to locate session files manually.
evidence: all wave-bro tasks in thread-935b467d show transcript_location=null
~/.bro-harness/sessions/a2eb6d49*.json = 412KB, 442 items, zero timestamp fields, contains compaction_summary (history rewritten)
orchestrator postmortem of slow waves had to reconstruct timing from usage arithmetic; retained-window tool calls: 82/133 = shell_poll (validates gap-c6dbc03f)
